candidates.exact_span: No limits are established if the receiving stream is not designated for the particular uses.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Use-designation applicability determines whether any numeric discharge limit is established for a parameter; if no limit is established, Purpose A has no enforceable limit to compare against measurements and Purpose B may treat related monitoring as not limit-driven.

candidates.locator: Page 28 / fact_sheet / STEP 3
candidates.exact_span: No limits are established if the potential instream w aste concentrations are less than the chronic w ater quality criteria.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of whether calculated instream waste concentrations are below chronic criteria determines whether an effluent limit is established at all, changing the applicable limit outcome for Purpose A.

candidates.locator: Page 28 / fact_sheet / STEP 3
candidates.exact_span: The most applicable stringent criteria are used to establish effluent limitations for a given parameter.
candidates.computation_change_reason: When multiple criteria columns apply to a pollutant, selection of the 'most applicable stringent' criterion changes the Cs value used in limit formulas and therefore the resulting numeric discharge limit.

candidates.locator: Page 28 / fact_sheet / STEP 3
candidates.exact_span: Water quality criteria apply at the end-of-pipe for acute aquatic life criteria and discharges to public lakes.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether acute aquatic life or public-lake conditions apply changes whether criteria are evaluated at end-of-pipe versus instream, altering which concentration basis and limit formula path governs the numeric limit.
